The Road to Evercold has begun, helping you prepare for the upcoming release of Evercold!
  • Our longest Free Login Campaign ever! Play free up to 30 days!
  • Tales of Adventure: Winter's Prelude available for a limited time!
A new Letter from the Producer from Producer and Director Naoki Yoshida has been published to mark the start of the promotion—be sure to check it out!

Free Login Campaign Schedule

From Monday, November 16, 2026 at 12:00 a.m. (PST) / 8:00 (GMT) / 19:00 (AEDT) to Thursday, January 14, 2027 at 6:59 a.m. (PST) / 14:59 (GMT) / Friday, 15 January 2027 at 1:59 (AEDT) As a token of our appreciation to players who have continued to support FFXIV and are not eligible for the Free Login Campaign, we will send a selection of items via the moogle delivery service. To receive the items, eligible players must log in before maintenance for the release of Patch 8.0 begins.

Tales of Adventure: Winter’s Prelude Availability Period

From Monday, November 16, 2026 at 12:00 a.m. (PST) / 8:00 (GMT) / 19:00 (AEDT) to the release of Patch 8.0 For Warriors of Light returning for adventure after completing the Hydaelyn and Zodiark saga, now is the perfect time to catch up ahead of Evercold! For a limited time, players who have completed the main scenario quest "Endwalker" can purchase Tales of Adventure: Winter's Prelude at a special price, allowing them to jump straight to Patch 7.5. Catch up on the latest story and prepare for the adventures to come in Evercold! Visit the Road to Evercold special site for details.

items.title: A paid Final Fantasy XIV item lets you skip Dawntrail
items.summary: Square Enix has introduced a rather surprising new item in its MMORPG’s in-game store. Final Fantasy XIV fans can now purchase Tales of Adventure: Winter’s…
items.content:
Square Enix has introduced a rather surprising new item in its MMORPG’s in-game store. Final Fantasy XIV fans can now purchase Tales of Adventure: Winter’s Prelude.

This item, which costs €6.99 , automatically completes the main story quests from Newfound Adventures (Update 6.1) through Into the Mist (Update 7.4). To be clear, this means players can thus completely skip the story of the Dawntrail expansion, which had received a rather lukewarm reception from fans. This will allow them to dive straight into the most recent content before the release of Evercold on February 23.

To use this item, you must have reached level 90, have access to all of the game’s expansions, and have completed the Endwalker quest.

items.title: Wisdom of Nym: Unanswered questions I have about Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold
Final Fantasy 14 really wants Evercold to be the expansion everyone comes back to, so much so it's giving you 30 days free gametime if you've been gone long enough
items.summary: Time to finish up that post-Dawntrail MSQ, folks.
items.content:
RPG Final Fantasy Final Fantasy 14 Final Fantasy 14 really wants Evercold to be the expansion everyone comes back to, so much so it's giving you 30 days free gametime if you've been gone long enough News By Mollie Taylor Published 16 November 2026 Time to finish up that post-Dawntrail MSQ, folks.

(Image credit: Square Enix) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Final Fantasy 14 is set to make some big changes when the upcoming expansion Evercold releases in February. An overhaul to combat, dailies, and new raid difficulties are set to shake things up and, hopefully, keep people sticking around for longer.

And judging by a recent Letter from the Producer , Naoki Yoshida really wants folks coming back to see what Evercold is all about. So much so that the game's offering 30 free days for long-gone adventurers… or a quick-and-dirty paid skip if you're so inclined.

"Encouraging players to return is no mean feat," Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such issues, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed."

I can only assume that for that reason, the decision's been made to offer up a $9 cash shop item that'll skip you through Endwalker's patch story, as well as all of Dawntrail up until the final story patch. Now Final Fantasy 14 has offered paid story skips in the past—it still does—but this is the first time it's explicitly offered one for the current expansion. Usually the skips'll stop dead before the current expansion, meaning you still need to play through the newest story.

It's a pretty niche paid skip, too. You'll need to have at least completed Endwalker's main story and have a level 90 job on your chosen character, and even then you'll still have to level up to 100 in your own time in order to tackle the final patch quest of Dawntrail. But worry not, if you haven't played the game in six months, you'll be able to snap up 30 days of free game time until January 14. Plenty of time to get a job to max level and prepare for Evercold.

Final Fantasy 14's ongoing pursuit in making its 500-hour story less daunting almost manifested into something in August, but Yoshi-P decided to postpone it Final Fantasy 14: Dawntrail's final story patch is exactly what the game needed, and has the 4-month wait for Evercold suddenly feeling a whole lot longer Final Fantasy 14: Evercold delayed to February, preorders start next week I'm mostly surprised by the introduction of this paid item because Yoshida has long been rather protective of the game's story. Something he admits in this very same letter: "I strongly believe that FF14 is a story-driven MMORPG," he wrote. "On top of that, skipping it all means you likely won't be familiar with the battle system and therefore will become a burden for other players in multiplayer content."

I do find it a little funny that Yoshida is worried that story skippers will weigh others down in dungeons and the like—I've played many a level 100 dungeon with folks who have clearly played enough to understand how to play yet still can't press their buttons properly.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

But anyway, Yoshida does admit that there is a lot of story to get through. "The Hydaelyn and Zodiark saga alone encompasses five expansions' worth of content," he wrote. "And with Dawntrail marking the start of the second saga, plus the coming addition of Evercold, the story continues to unfold into something even larger."

It really does feel like Square Enix wants Evercold to mark a big resurgence for the game, one I really do hope pays off for the developer. I've been playing off-and-on since A Realm Reborn and have seen just about every evolution the game has taken, and also the ways it has stagnated over time. Its confidence in trying to draw people back has me excited for the changes that are coming.

Mollie Taylor Social Links Navigation Features Producer Mollie spent her early childhood deeply invested in games like Killer Instinct, Toontown and Audition Online, which continue to form the pillars of her personality today. She joined PC Gamer in 2020 as a news writer and now lends her expertise to write a wealth of features, guides and reviews with a dash of chaos. She can often be found causing mischief in Final Fantasy 14, using those experiences to write neat things about her favourite MMO. When she's not staring at her bunny girl she can be found sweating out rhythm games, pretending to be good at fighting games or spending far too much money at her local arcade.

items.title: FF14 Free Trial Extended To Lapsed Players Ahead Of Evercold
items.summary: In preparation for Evercold, Square Enix is giving away 30 days of free game time to eligible players and has a new item for purchase that'll let you skip Dawntrail
items.content:
If you are like me and haven’t played Final Fantasy XIV in a minute, now might be the time to jump back in and finally get through Dawntrail before the new expansion launches in 2027. Starting November 16, players who haven’t logged in to the paid MMORPG in the last five months (150 days specifically) are eligible for 30 days of free playtime.

Players have from November 16th to January 14, 2027 to claim their free 30 days, which means that, if you time it right, your free period will overlap with the launch of the $45 Evercold expansion on February 23. Square Enix has all the specifics here .

The Road to Evercold begins today, helping you prepare for the upcoming release of Evercold!

⭐ 30-day Free Login Campaign ⭐ Tales of Adventure: Winter's Prelude

— FINAL FANTASY XIV (@en.finalfantasyxiv.com) 2026-11-16T10:30:05.686Z

Digging into the details, it seems like Square Enix knows a lot of people (including me) lit out after Endwalker and haven’t been back to play the latest expansion, Dawntrail. In addition to offering free game time, Square Enix is also offering a new $10 Tales of Adventure item which lets players auto-skip main story quest content. It’s designed specifically to leap-frog players over Dawntrail stuff, taking them from the end of Endwalker to the beginning of “In Fate’s Footsteps,” this year’s Evercold -introducing 7.5 event patch.

It is powerfully seductive to pay $10 bucks to take the coward’s way out of Dawntrail . I’ve heard that expansion is just okay, and possibly even worth skipping. But I play Final Fantasy XIV for its story. It can’t always be Heavensward or Shadowbringers , sometimes there has to be a Stormblood in there and that’s okay. As I try to take advantage of the free game time, I’ll finally see Dawntrail for myself.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Players Mourn The Primals Bassist With In-Game Funerals and Gatherings
items.summary: Final Fantasy XIV players are paying tribute to the bassist of the game’s official band, mourning him and celebrating his legacy with virtual, in-game funerals across servers worldwide.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV players are paying tribute to the bassist of the game’s official band, mourning him and celebrating his legacy with virtual, in-game funerals across servers worldwide.

Eikichi Iwai was the bass guitarist for The Primals, a band formed specifically to make some of the music in Square Enix’s extremely popular MMORPG. While they aren’t the only ones responsible for some of the game’s iconic tunes, they’re certainly some of the most notable, and they’ve become a firm fixture in the Final Fantasy fanbase over the years.

Iwai’s death was officially announced on November 11, 2026 by his own rock band, Chirinuruwowa, and the Final Fantasy XIV development team, the latter of which penned a public letter to fans informing them of the news.

“As announced earlier today, we are deeply saddened to share the news of the sudden passing of bassist Eikichi Iwai,” the statement reads. “Having witnessed his truly unforgettable performance on stage at the recent FINAL FANTASY XIV Fan Festival in Japan, the sudden news of his passing has come as a profound shock. The members of THE PRIMALS and the entire FFXIV Development and Operations teams are overcome with deep sorrow.

“As we reflect on all that Eikichi-san has left behind, our thoughts are with him, and we offer our heartfelt condolences.”

Chirinuruwowa published a similar statement on social media. “We regret to inform you that our bassist, Iwaieikichi, has passed away suddenly,” the group wrote. “The sudden news of his passing has left all of us in the band and on the staff struggling to come to terms with it, and we are deeply saddened.” The band also informed fans that all upcoming performances in their Endless Loop 2026 -Public- tour have been cancelled.

Iwai's death sent shockwaves throughout the FFXIV playerbase. In acknowledgement of his legacy as a performer and paying tribute to his contributions to the game, these players gathered together within their respective servers to hold virtual funerals in some of the MMORPG’s fantastical locales.

For example, players on the European server Omega formed a circle around Limsa Lominsa’s Aetheryte Plaza, lighting campfires in remembrance of the bassist. And in the Sephirot, Materia DC server, players hung out for more than seven hours at Ultima Thule, calmly sitting in its field of flowers.

Fans, content creators, and fellow members of the games industry have shared their own fond memories of the game and the impact Iwai's music had on their lives.

@FF_XIV_EN A small memorial for Eikichi Iwai on Omega (Chaos). Thank you for everything, Iwai-san. Your final performance at Tokyo Fan Fest was incredible Chaos DC・オメガでイワイエイキチさんを偲ぶ小さな集まりを開きます。 イワイさん、ありがとう。東京ファンフェスでの最後の演奏最高でした https://t.co/2204TnVxIU

Somehow some people are still here 7 hours later (I've just been doing other stuff) I'll just leave my character here overnight as I'm going to sleep if anyone wants to continue the memorial feel free to come here at Ultima Thule, Sephirot, Materia DC #THEPRIMALS #ffxiv https://t.co/l0YB7Ny45Q

イワイエイキチさん いつも素晴らしいエネルギッシュなLIVEをありがとうございました イフリート鯖のイフリートの祭壇 (X35.2 Y19.8)の追悼の場からお悔やみ申し上げます #FF14 #THEPRIMALS https://t.co/Mi2oJtMiS5

“This one truly hurts… Words just can't describe the shock and grief I'm feeling right now,” YouTuber and game composer Alex Moukala wrote . “FFXIV fans lost an absolute icon. Many bass players around the world lost a hero. And those who knew Eikichi-san personally lost an incredibly kind friend. Rest in peace, Eikichi-san.”

“Eikichi-san was an absolute legend. This is so sudden and devastating. My sincere condolences to his family and friends. May he rest in peace,” another fan said .

items.title: Fans Gather In Final Fantasy XIV In Memorial For Eikichi Iwai, Bassist For The Primals
items.summary: His passing comes days after he performed at Fan Fest Japan 2026
items.content:
Eikichi Iwai, bassist in the Primals, the official band for Final Fantasy XIV , has passed away. Square Enix and Final Fantasy XIV accounts announced the news of his passing on social media. “We are deeply saddened to share the news of the sudden passing of bassist Eikichi Iwai,” the announcement said . In the wake of Iwai’s passing, memorials are popping up across multiple FFXIV servers as fans remember him and the music he was part of.

In addition to Iwai, the band is led by Final Fantasy FFXIV composer Masayoshi Soken and features musician Gunn on guitar, Tetsuya Tachibana on drums, and Michael-Christopher Koji Fox on vocals. Fans might recognize Koji Fox as being the English localization and translation director for a number of Final Fantasy games.

Much like Nobuo Uematsu’s band the Black Mages, the Primals are known for their rock arrangements and original music for the Final Fanasy XIV soundtrack. W anna hear a rock version of “ Flow “? They got you. You wanna start crying at 10:30 in the morning like I am? “Footfalls” is good for that. I’ll be the first to admit “ To the Edge ” is not one of my favorites out of the Primals’ catalogue (please don’t hurt me), but even I can’t deny Iwai’s sick-ass bass line. His bass makes that song and every one of the Primals’ songs. Iwai’s loss will be profoundly felt.

Square Enix holds Final Fantasy Fan Fests across the world every year featuring a performance by the Primals as one of the main attractions. Iwai’s final performance was at Fan Fest Japan earlier this month, and you can watch a portion of that performance here .

“Going to have The Primals on the whole time I’m playing tonight,” read a comment in the FFXIV subreddit. “Rest easy, Eikichi, thank you for all those basslines.”

items.title: Several Final Fantasy XIV Modding Communities Have Banned Popular NSFW Modder
items.summary: The bans came after modder Noffletoff was credibly accused of participating in graphic discussions of illegal content
items.content:
Several major Final Fantasy XIV modding communities have taken steps to remove the work of a popular not-safe-for-work mod creator after chat logs were exposed in which the modder was seen participating in graphic discussions of illegal material.

Content warning for discussion of child abuse sexual assault material (CSAM)

On YouTube, a user identified as Chunni Doll posted a video alleging that modder Noffletoff, along with several other Final Fantasy XIV players, was engaged in the discussion and sharing of CSAM. The video claims that the chats took place in an invite-only chat room that was part of a larger Matrix server centered on loli/shotacon content. (Sometimes described as an alternative to Discord, Matrix servers are decentralized servers that allow for real-time communication.)

The video was accompanied by a Proton document in which screenshots of the chatlogs are displayed. Kotaku has reviewed the document, and while direct references to victims’ names and explicit descriptions of CSAM content have been censored, the alleged participants can be seen making references to content they’ve watched and potentially sharing content with users on another platform called Session. Matrix administrators were made aware of the server and it was shut down and the alleged participants banned.

Noffletoff is the creator of several paid Final Fantasy XI V body and animation mods that are widely used to create NSFW FFXIV content. As a result of these allegations, numerous FFXIV modding communities are purging his work from their platforms. Additionally, Noffletoff’s Patreon and X account have been deleted.

The Final Fantasy XIV Mod Archive (XMA), one of the largest hosting sites of FFXIV mods, has banned the account associated with Noffletoff. Kotaku has reviewed messages sent in the XMA Discord server confirming Noffletoff’s suspension, a decision announced by a moderator after a user asked what would be done in light of the allegations. “I think it’s reasonable at this point to go ahead and suspend Noff’s account (and have done so),” the post read.

Kotaku has also reviewed messages in Booty Bay, a Discord server associated with pirating FFXIV mods. The moderators of that Discord server have taken similar action, removing his mods from their repositories while banning them from future uploads and banning all discussions related to the allegations against Noffletoff. Snowcloak, a Final Fantasy XIV mod program that allows users to view other players’ mods in game, will block the display of Noffletoff’s mods. “Users attempting to use these mods will receive a warning that the file is blocked,” read a message from a Snowcloak moderator, according to screenshots from the server reviewed by Kotaku .

According to the video, the alleged participants have been reported to authorities. Kotaku has reached out to Square Enix for comment.
